title: German football's fan membership figures continue to climb
content: The Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 are home to some incredible fan membership figures. The Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 continue to have some of the best supported clubs in the game, with recent figures showing an increase in club memberships in both leagues and Bayern Munich announcing a new world record total. Bayern confirmed at their 2025 annual general meeting at the start of November that they had reached 432,500 members to make them the largest sports club in the world by membership - an achievement president Herbert Hainer said "we can be proud of". It's a huge increase on the 400,000 number they announced to mark the club's 125th anniversary in February, which took them level with Benfica of Portugal, and the total of 382,000 at the previous year's AGM. Dr Hubertus Hess-Grunewald, president and chairman of the supervisory board at Werder, meanwhile, also announced in 2025 when the club reached 64,000 members - of which over 1,000 have been members for life - that "We are incredibly proud of how our membership numbers have grown.

content: SV Werder Bremen is a German multi-sport club based in Bremen, founded on 4 February 1899 as FV Werder Bremen by a group of young enthusiasts who had won a football in a tug-of-war competition and began playing on the Stadtwerder meadows.](#ref-1) Renamed SV Werder Bremen in 1920 to encompass additional sports like handball and athletics, the club is predominantly renowned for its professional football team, which has been a founding member of the Bundesliga since 1963 and currently competes in Germany's top division.](#ref-2) With a rich history spanning over 125 years, Werder Bremen symbolizes the city's pride and maintains a strong family-oriented identity despite its large fanbase, fostering a vibrant atmosphere on match days that unites the community.](#ref-1) The club's football section has achieved significant success, securing four Bundesliga championships in the seasons 1964/65, 1987/88, 1992/93, and 2003/04, along with six DFB-Pokal (German Cup) victories in 1960/61, 1990/91, 1993/94, 1998/99, 2003/04, and 2008/09.](#ref-3) Internationally, Werder Bremen won the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup in 1991/92 and has participated in various European competitions, including reaching the UEFA Cup final in 2008/09.](#ref-3) Notable eras include the tenure of manager Otto Rehhagel from 1981 to 1995, during which the team claimed two league titles, two domestic cups, and the European Cup Winners' Cup, and the long-serving Thomas Schaaf, who led the club to a domestic double in 2003/04 and another cup win in 2009.](#ref-2) Iconic players such as Claudio Pizarro, the all-time top scorer with 109 Bundesliga goals for the club, and Mesut Özil have further elevated its legacy.](#ref-2) Werder Bremen's home matches are played at the Weserstadion, a historic venue opened in 1930 and located on the banks of the Weser River, which has a capacity of around 42,000 and serves as a central hub for the club's activities.](#ref-1) Beyond football, the title: SV Werder Bremen - Wikipedia
content: # SV Werder Bremen. Founded on 4 February 1899, Werder are best known for their professional association football team, who compete in the Bundesliga, the first tier of the German football league system. Bremen share the record for most seasons played in the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich, and are ranked third in the all-time Bundesliga table, only behind Bayern and Borussia Dortmund. The team's first major trophy was the 1960–61 DFB-Pokal; they last won the cup in 2008–09. Bremen's first German championship came in 1964–65, and their latest in 2003–04, when they won the double "Double (association football)"). In European football, Werder won the 1991–92 European Cup Winners' Cup, and were runners-up in the 2008–09 UEFA Cup. Bremen have played at the Weserstadion since 1909. In 1900, the club was one of the founder members of the German Football Association (DFB). Between the end of the Second World War and the formation of the Bundesliga in 1963, the club was recognised as one of the top two teams in northern Germany, along with Hamburger SV.
